timeline.body: The Strait of Hormuz narrows to 24 miles between Iran and Oman — roughly one-fifth of the world's oil passes through it daily, giving Iran a chokepoint over the global economy.

CIA and MI6 overthrew Iran's democratically elected Prime Minister Mohammad Mosaddegh after he nationalized British oil assets, installing Shah Pahlavi as a Western-aligned autocrat and creating the foundational grievance of US-Iran relations.
Britain withdrew from all military bases east of Suez, leaving a power vacuum in the Persian Gulf that the US filled by arming the Shah as its regional policeman under the Nixon Doctrine.
The Iranian Revolution toppled the Shah and replaced America's closest Middle Eastern ally with an Islamic Republic built on opposition to both the US and Israel.

Iraq invaded Iran with US intelligence support and Gulf state financing — Saudi Arabia and Kuwait bankrolled Saddam's war effort with an estimated $60 billion while the West supplied dual-use chemicals later used in poison gas attacks.
The Tanker War saw Iran and Iraq attack over 450 merchant vessels in the Persian Gulf, first establishing Iran's doctrine of threatening Hormuz shipping when cornered.

USS Vincennes shot down Iran Air Flight 655 over the Strait of Hormuz, killing all 290 civilians aboard — the US never formally apologized, and the incident remains seared into Iranian collective memory.
Operation Praying Mantis destroyed half of Iran's operational navy in a single day, the largest American naval engagement since World War II.

Iranian dissidents revealed secret uranium enrichment facilities at Natanz that Tehran had hidden from inspectors for 18 years, triggering the nuclear crisis that has driven US-Iran confrontation ever since.

Iran sent Washington a secret proposal offering to negotiate on its nuclear program, support for Hezbollah and Hamas, and a two-state solution — the Bush administration, emboldened by Baghdad's fall, never replied.
Stuxnet, a cyberweapon jointly built by the US and Israel, destroyed roughly 1,000 Iranian centrifuges at Natanz — the first known digital attack to cause physical destruction.
The JCPOA nuclear deal traded Iranian enrichment limits and international inspections for sanctions relief, the closest the US and Iran had come to détente since 1979.
Trump withdrew the US from the JCPOA despite Iran's verified compliance, reimposing maximum pressure sanctions that collapsed Iran's currency while pushing Tehran to resume high-level enrichment.

A US drone strike killed Qasem Soleimani, commander of Iran's Quds Force and architect of its entire regional proxy network, at Baghdad airport — Iran retaliated by striking US bases in Iraq with ballistic missiles.

The Abraham Accords normalized relations between Israel, the UAE, Bahrain, and others, building a formal anti-Iran axis across the Middle East that sidelined the Palestinian cause as a precondition for diplomacy.
China brokered a surprise Saudi-Iran diplomatic restoration after seven years of severed ties, briefly suggesting a regional order beyond American mediation.

Iran and Israel struck each other's territory directly for the first time — Iran launched over 300 drones and missiles in April, Israel hit Iranian air defenses in October — ending decades of conflict waged solely through proxies.
